executive_summary: Websites: 3 of 4 already protect their traffic with hybrid post-quantum key exchange; 1 still uses classical key exchange only (recorded pq_tls results from 2026-10-05 (sample-results.json), not a live check). Northwind is fictional, so these are four real public websites checked on 2026-10-05 as stand-ins, not Northwind's own.
Code and configuration: 37 uses of cryptography in 12 of 12 files. 16 are weak today, 17 would be broken by a large quantum computer, 2 are only weakened, 2 are fine.
Under the planning assumption z = 9 years (an assumption, not a forecast), 3 of 5 systems are already late: ERP (SAP), Supplier EDI feed, Inventory API (customer orders).
Do now: ERP (SAP): replace cryptography that is weak today, and 7 more.
Certificates everywhere still use RSA or elliptic curves, like every web certificate today; that migration waits for post-quantum certificates to become available.

assumptions.z_source: ASSUMPTION for this case study: z = 9 years (2026 to 2035, the year NIST IR 8547's initial public draft proposes for disallowing quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms). A planning horizon, NOT a forecast of when a quantum computer will exist.
assumptions.x_source: ASSUMPTION: 10 years of required confidentiality when a system does not say; replace per system.
assumptions.y_source: ASSUMPTION: 5 years to migrate when a system does not say; large estates often need longer.
